quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of these driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?

options.text: Alertness and concentration.
Reaction time and coordination.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down your nervous system. It makes you less alert, harder to concentrate, slower to react, and much less coordinated.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass. The side with the broken line can cross and pass. The side with the solid line cannot.

questions.question: You should not start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red:

options.text: Under any circumstances.
Unless you entered on a yellow light.
Unless you entered on a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Under any circumstances.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. If you block the intersection, you can get a ticket.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. You should drive:

options.text: Close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Farther behind the truck than you would behind a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you follow too close to a truck, the driver cannot see you in his mirrors. You need more space behind a truck than behind a regular car to stay safe.

questions.question: When parking next to a curb, you should use your turn signals:

options.text: Only when leaving the curb.
Only when moving to the curb, not when leaving.
When moving to the curb and when leaving the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When moving to the curb and when leaving the curb.
questions.explanation: Always signal when moving to a curb or leaving a curb.

questions.question: If your car breaks down on the highway, you should:

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Move completely off the road with all four wheels, if possible.
Stop wherever you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely off the road with all four wheels, if possible.
questions.explanation: When your vehicle breaks down, move it completely off the road if you can. Keep all four wheels off the main part of the highway.

questions.question: Head restraints should be:

options.text: Adjusted so they touch the back of your head.
Removed from the seats if possible.
Left anywhere, since they do not matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjusted so they touch the back of your head.
questions.explanation: Head restraints protect you from whiplash if someone hits your car from behind. Adjust them to touch the back of your head.

questions.question: Fatigue increases the risk of:

options.text: Missing an exit.
Being late for an appointment.
Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Falling asleep at the wheel and crashing.
questions.explanation: When you are tired, you cannot judge speed and distance well. You could fall asleep at the wheel and crash, which can hurt or kill you and others.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through flooded water. Even if it looks shallow, it can hide dangers. Turn around and find a different way.

questions.question: If bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see well, increase the space between you and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you might not see coming.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction because of water on the road, what should you do?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to get better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to stop your vehicle from sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When driving in heavy rain, even at 30 mph, your tires may lose contact with the road and slide on a layer of water. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not use the brakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You can travel in either direction in this lane.
Traffic is moving in two directions on this road.
You are approaching a divided highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is moving in two directions on this road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic is moving in two directions on this road.

questions.question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You cannot turn in the direction the arrow shows.
You may turn in the direction the arrow shows after you stop.
You may turn in the direction the arrow shows.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot turn in the direction the arrow shows.
questions.explanation: A steady red arrow means you cannot go in that direction. You must stop and wait for a green signal before you can proceed.

questions.question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?

options.text: It is illegal to turn off your signal before completing the turn.
It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Always signal when turning, changing lanes, slowing down, or stopping. This tells other drivers, motorcycle riders, cyclists, and pedestrians what you intend to do.

questions.question: When passing another car, you have enough space to return to the driving lane:

options.text: When the other driver signals for you to move back into the lane.
When you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.
When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before moving back into the driving lane, make sure there is a safe gap between your car and the passed car. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to move back into the lane.

questions.question: What word appears on a red octagon-shaped sign?

options.text: Do not enter.
One-way.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: An eight-sided sign always means stop. You must come to a complete stop at this sign.

questions.question: You hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked vehicle or damage property, you must leave a note on the vehicle with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to know where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. You do not need to stop.

questions.question: When should you not use your horn?

options.text: When you cannot see far ahead.
When you might hit another vehicle.
Near blind pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near blind pedestrians.
questions.explanation: Do not use your horn near blind pedestrians because it may be dangerous. Yield to the pedestrian and go when it is safe.

questions.question: After a train passes at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Wait for the signal lights to stop flashing.
Look for a second train.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: After a train passes, another train may be coming on a different track. Do not drive until all gates are up and all warning lights have stopped flashing.

questions.question: When a school bus stops to load or unload children, you must:

options.text: Stop completely until all children leave the bus.
Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
Change lanes, drive slowly, and pass the bus carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has flashing red lights and its stop arm out, you must stop completely. Wait until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is pulled back before driving. Even when the bus moves, make sure no children are in the road before you proceed.

questions.question: Where are U-turns not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road where you can see 500 feet ahead in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians, which could cause a crash.

questions.question: Hard braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, so you cannot steer.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, so you cannot steer.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice locks the front wheels and causes you to lose steering control. Drive slowly and avoid hard braking.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, you should:

options.text: Release the gas pedal.
Brake as hard as possible.
Turn off the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, release the gas or brake pedal to regain control. Steer toward the direction of the skid to straighten out the vehicle.
